claims.text: The United States and Denmark announced a security agreement regarding Greenland to resolve a diplomatic dispute.
Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that Denmark would grant the US permanent control over security, and all other needs in Greenland at no cost to the United States.
The security deal between the US, Denmark, and Greenland is expected to be signed next week at the UN General Assembly.
A US State Department official stated the agreement bans non-NATO countries from building military bases in Greenland or making investments in sensitive sectors.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen stated the agreement strengthens common security in the Arctic and North Atlantic while recognizing the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination.
French President Emmanuel Macron stated that the agreement reaffirms Danish sovereignty over Greenland and respects international law.
Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen called the deal a binding agreement that strengthens security while respecting Denmark's red lines.
Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen stated the agreement recognizes Greenland's interests and is to the benefit of all parties.
Greenland has a population of roughly 56,000 residents, with more than two-thirds of its territory lying within the Arctic Circle.
The United States operates Pituffik Space Base in northwestern Greenland under the Defense of Greenland Treaty signed in 1951.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the agreement a historic deal that permanently and completely addresses US national security concerns.
Donald Trump first floated the idea of buying Greenland from Denmark in 2019 during his first term as US president.
In January 2026, Donald Trump indicated the US could use force to seize Greenland.
US President Donald Trump announced plans to form an AI Force and appoint an artificial intelligence czar.
Donald Trump stated that artificial intelligence could eventually account for as much as 25% of the United States' GDP.
Tech executives including Dario Amodei of Anthropic, Sam Altman of OpenAI, and Elon Musk of xAI have advocated for a slowdown or regulations in AI development.
The UK Parliament's Joint Committee on Human Rights published a report calling for a new AI bill to address risks posed by the technology.
Donald Trump stated on social media that candidates for the proposed AI Czar position must be high IQ individuals.
California Governor Gavin Newsom announced plans for a panel to develop AI safety regulations, including a potential kill switch for misaligned AI programs.
An Anthropic researcher warned that AI companies are gambling with lives and that AI could pose existential risks to humanity by the end of the decade.
Former US AI czar David Sacks resigned earlier in the year and currently chairs Trump's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.
The US House of Representatives passed a bill in a 417 to 3 vote to minimize the impact of AI data center electricity usage on residents' utility bills.
US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are scheduled to meet at the White House on September 24, with AI competition expected to be discussed.
Donald Trump stated his administration will not hinder or stifle the growth of the AI industry but will use existing criminal and civil laws to target bad actors.
Iran-backed Houthi militants launched drone and ballistic missile attacks targeting the Saudi capital Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu.
A column of black smoke rose from fuel tanks near King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, leading to temporary flight delays and cancellations.
Saudi authorities intercepted a ballistic missile over Riyadh and stopped hostile aerial attempts over Bish, Taif, Farasan, and Yanbu.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya al-Sarea stated the attacks were in response to 300 Saudi strikes across Yemen over the past week.
Fighting between Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces in Yemen claimed 48 lives on Saturday, including 31 Houthi fighters and 17 government soldiers.
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan stated Turkiye would consider how to support Saudi Arabia under a trilateral defence pact signed in Mecca on August 7.
Pakistani military spokesperson Lieutenant-General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry stated Pakistan would physically defend Saudi Arabia to any extent under the Mecca Defence Alliance.
The United Nations reported that renewed fighting in Yemen has displaced over 112,000 people.
The United States approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia.
Iranian Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei stated Tehran wants the Saudi-Houthi war to end.
The UN Security Council issued a statement condemning Houthi attacks on Saudi civilian and energy infrastructure.
The Houthis recently seized control of the port of Mokha, Perim Island, and the Red Sea islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish.
